prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a hit while turning left in Houston, Texas, and has neck and back strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1374; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather not give my full name on a recording, but you can use the claim reference.

Q: That's fine. Can you tell me where you were and what you were doing when the collision happened?

A: I was driving through an intersection in Houston, Texas, turning left onto a side street. The light had turned yellow and I was trying to clear the intersection.

Q: Which direction were you traveling, and what did you see of the other vehicle?

A: I was heading east and wanted to turn north. I saw an SUV coming from the west, but I thought it was going to stop. It didn't slow down much at all, and it hit the front passenger side of my car.

Q: Did you have your turn signal on?

A: Yes, I had it on for a good stretch before I started the turn.

Q: Were you wearing your seatbelt, and did the airbags deploy?

A: Seatbelt, yes. The airbags did not go off, but the belt locked up hard and pushed me back into the seat.

Q: Did you go to a doctor or an emergency room after the accident?

A: I went to an urgent care clinic that same afternoon. They said I had a neck strain and a lower back strain. My neck is stiff when I turn my head, and my lower back aches after sitting for more than twenty minutes.

Q: Are you still receiving treatment?

A: Yes, I have physical therapy twice a week and I'm taking over-the-counter pain relievers. My doctor wants me to keep going for now.

Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?

A: Only that I was driving carefully and I believe the other driver should have yielded. I'm willing to provide my medical records if you need them.

Q: Thank you. This concludes the recorded statement.
